items.text: Programs run in a persisted pane are no longer put in Windows efficiency mode, so a big burst of output is as fast as in a plain pane.
The session manager now adopts an in-app update instead of claiming it is "replacing itself" forever.
The session agent's idle CPU drops by about 45%: its once-a-second process-table walk is cheaper and shared.
The session agent's idle CPU drops by another two-thirds: the app no longer asks its own machine's agent to watch every process each second.
The session agent batches a flood at the ConPTY read: agent CPU over a 64 MB flood drops ~28%.
